Ruling: interface gap; the reply inverts the interface. k1p.screened is true by construction and carries the K-1's refusals (the refusal list of forms/2025/k1p.yaml, each `when:` a gate such as k1p.not_at_risk_if_loss); every person.k1p_* sum filters on it, so a refused K-1 refuses the return. The reply builds a predicate that is true when a refusal applies, the opposite of the label 'passed every screen', and omits the trader, tests 4/6/7 and former-passive refusals. Triage: 109/534 agree; 171 project-refuses, 71 project-unknown, 183 value (the inversion). Same reading as the first-round ruling of this line.

Ruling: model error; the line is 'This Schedule K-1 passed every screen (true; the refusals of a K-1 are told here)', true on a supported K-1 with the refusals declared on it; the reply defines the inverse ('This Schedule K-1 has items the tool does not support'), false on every supported K-1 (186 value differences, e.g. x2k1p.fk2_general_material, fk7_portfolio_only), and omits the trader, tests 4/6/7, former passive, prior_not_active and se_loss_not_material screens. Not a project defect: the project's refusals are its declared scope (form note). triage 87/523 agree (26 fixtures, 497 partial records; no generated return reaches k1p while scope.k1 refuses K-1 filers); differing: 157 project-refuses, 93 project-unknown, 186 value.

Ruling: model error; as the earlier rulings, the line is 'This Schedule K-1 passed every screen (true; the refusals of a K-1 are told here)', true by construction with the K-1's refusals declared on it; the reply defines the inverse (true when any screening input is Yes). executable triage (.transcription/triage/2025/k1p.json, this pass): 209/796 agree; differences {"project-refuses": 38, "project-unknown": 118, "value": 431}; on completed returns {"project-unknown": 67, "value": 237}.
